title: Actor-aware parameter schema and graceful error protocol for tool calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood scales tool/function calling across hosted, dedicated, and private modes we see two classes of production failures: (1) malformed/ambiguous parameters produced by models that cause downstream tool exceptions (type errors, missing keys, unexpected enum values) and (2) brittle SDK/runtime behavior when parameter errors are surfaced to customers (opaque 500s, inconsistent HTTP error codes, and no recovery guidance).

Goal: Define a compact, actor-aware JSON schema format for function/tool parameter contracts plus a succinct error taxonomy and runtime mapping that (a) enables deterministic validation pre-dispatch, (b) surfaces human-friendly, actionable error messages and remediation hints, and (c) supports graceful fallback policies (syntactic repair, soft-retry, model variant routing). This ticket covers the schema additions, validator semantics, error codes, and a rollout plan with compatibility guards for older clients and tools.
proposal_summary: Introduce an extended JSON schema envelope that includes an optional 'actor' field (requestor vs. model), explicit coercion modes, and an 'exampleHints' member for runtime repair heuristics. Implement server-side validation stages: parse -> lightweight schema check -> semantic checks (uniqueness, cross-field dependencies) -> canonicalization/coercion. Return a structured, stable error envelope with error_code, human_message, machine_hint and optional repair_script. Add observability: tokenized error labels emitted as metrics and traces. Document migration/compatibility behaviour and provide an SDK helper to perform local preflight validation.
design_notes:
Key design trade-offs: keep the schema extension backward-compatible with existing call manifests; avoid heavyweight full JSON Schema to reduce runtime CPU; provide opt-in strictness levels (lenient|strict) per customer route. Actor field lets us apply different coercion heuristics for assistant-generated parameters vs. user-provided context (e.g., prefer conservative coercion for user input). Repair scripts are only advisory strings (not executed server-side) to prevent remote code execution risks. Validation should run in <1ms median for typical 3-field tool calls.

Schema sketch (informal): {
  name: string,
  description: string,
  params: { type: "object", properties: {...}, required: [...], additionalProperties: false },
  actor: "model" | "user" | "system" (optional),
  coercion: "none" | "coerce_types" | "coerce_with_hints",
  exampleHints: [string],
  version: string
}

We will provide a compact validator implemented in Rust (runtime) and a JS reference for local SDK pre-validation.
acceptance_criteria: API: Server accepts new schema envelope and enforces versioned validation rules for runtime-2.4 routes.

Validation: For lenient routes, obvious type coercions (string->number if numeric string) are performed and logged; for strict routes, coercion returns a structured error without dispatching the tool.
Errors: Runtime returns the stable error envelope fields: error_code, human_message, machine_hint, severity, and suggested_repair (when available).
SDK: JS SDK exposes preflight.validateToolCall(manifest, params) that mirrors server checks and maps server error_codes to local exceptions.
Telemetry: Produce metrics for validation.failures by error_code and route, and add trace spans for validation steps.
Compatibility: Existing manifests without the new fields continue to work unchanged (default coercion=none).
error_taxonomy: INVALID_JSON: input could not be parsed as JSON (client-visible, high-level guidance to reformat)
MISSING_REQUIRED: required parameter missing (machine_hint includes missing key list)
TYPE_MISMATCH: value present but wrong primitive type (machine_hint suggests expected type and coercion possibility)
ENUM_VIOLATION: value not in allowed enum set (human_message includes allowed values)
SEMANTIC_CONFLICT: cross-field rule violated (e.g., start_time after end_time)
COERCION_REFUSED: runtime refused to coerce under strict mode
INTERNAL_VALIDATOR_ERROR: internal failure (should map to 5xx with safe fallback guidance)
runtime_mapping: HTTP mapping guidance: 400 for INVALID_JSON/MISSING_REQUIRED/TYPE_MISMATCH/ENUM_VIOLATION/CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION/ADDITIONAL_PROPERTY; 422 for SEMANTIC_CONFLICT; 409 for COERCION_REFUSED when a strictness change is negotiable; 500 for INTERNAL_VALIDATOR_ERROR. Always return the stable error envelope in the response body and include X-Redwood-Validation-Code header for fast routing on the client.
compatibility_plan: Phased rollout: (1) Canary routes for internal customers (one region) with validation telemetry; (2) opt-in for enterprise customers (console flag) with default lenient coercion; (3) GA with default coercion=none for public hosted API. Provide 'compatibility-mode' header allowing clients to request legacy behaviour. Deprecation window: 6 months for 'legacy' manifest shape followed by strong warnings in console and SDKs.
sdk_changes: JS SDK: add preflight.validateToolCall(manifest, params, options) -> {valid:boolean, errors: [error_envelope]}; Rust runtime: integrate compact validator crate and feature-flag the new envelope. Provide polyfill in python SDK that calls remote preflight endpoint when local validator not present.
test_plan: Unit tests for validator rules (positive/negative), fuzz tests against malformed/generated params, integration tests covering lenient/strict routes, property-based tests for coercion heuristics. Add synthetic incidents to chaos infra to confirm graceful fallback to model-variant routing when validation latency spikes.
rollout_steps: 1) Merge schema and validator crate (feature flag); 2) Deploy canary to us-west-2 for runtime-2.4 routes; 3) Monitor validation.metrics.* and validation.latency; 4) Enable opt-in in console for selected customers; 5) Public GA after two weeks of stable metrics.
